scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The style emerged in the 2000s in the southern suburbs of Paris, France, particularly at the Metropolis nightclub.
In 2002, Cyril Blanc and Alexandre Barouzdin organised 'Tecktonik Killer' parties under their project 'Tecktonik Events' to promote hardstyle and jumpstyle music from Belgium and the Netherlands.
Blanc noted the name was a pun on tectonic plates.

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: Electro dance emphasises arm movements, drawing from glowsticking techniques such as freehand patterns, the figure eight, and the leading hand concept.
It incorporates disco-inspired poses, angular movements, shuffling steps, and toprock or b-boy-style footwork.
Dancers use hips, knees, and feet smoothly or irregularly in time with the music.
Watch for Freehand glowsticking pattern.

Formation: club floors, street gatherings ('aprems'), and battle circles

scenes.title: Listen
narration: Typically performed to fast-paced techno and electro house music, often imported from Northern Europe, along with hardstyle and jumpstyle genres.
Listen for the synthesizers, electronic drum machines.
The pulse is 4/4.
Driving, heavy electronic synthesizer riffs combined with pounding four-on-the-floor kick drums imported from Northern Europe, designed for relentless high-energy club dancing.
